thread:
Maya (AE): HealthNode POC: they want PrivateLink from 5 accounts, must keep per-client IP for audits, need split-horizon DNS, firewall allowlist, and a rough monthly cost for ~12 TB. Can we support without major changes?

Liu (NetEng): PrivateLink works across accounts but endpoint ENI IPs become the source seen by backend. Native L3 client IP not preserved.

Tariq (Solutions): Options: (A) VPC peering between consumer and service VPCs -> preserves source IP but more routing work, ACLs, and peering approvals; (B) PrivateLink + per-account proxy agent that logs client IP locally and forwards with X-Forwarded-For; (C) Customer-hosted Private Deploy so logs keep original IP.

Maya (AE): They said cert-based identity might be OK instead of IP. Will that be acceptable for auditors?

Svetlana (Security): mTLS + client certs provide strong identity binding. If auditors accept identity + request trace, we can avoid L3 IP requirement. Need NDA to share SOC2 artifacts.

Hana (Pricing): Quick sketch: 12 TB ≈ 12,288 GB. At $0.015/GB => ~$185/mo data processing. Interface endpoints ~$0.01-0.02/hr => ~$7-15/mo each. For 5 endpoints add ~$35-75/mo. If we add NAT EIP pool for stable allowlist, NAT GW costs add hundreds depending on throughput.

Liu (NetEng): DNS: if endpoints created in each account, AWS makes private DNS entries by default. Alternatively, Route53 private hosted zones or Resolver rules for split-horizon. We'll document the simplest setup.

Tariq (Solutions): If they need stable source IPs to allowlist, recommended pattern: route egress through our transit NAT EIPs (we provide small static pool) or do VPC peering. Each has tradeoffs in cost and ops.

Maya (AE): Action items: 1) Liu to drop a 1-pager with peering vs endpoint vs proxy tradeoffs. 2) Hana to post a small cost table for 12TB + endpoints + optional NAT. 3) I'll ask customer if app-level identity (mTLS + header) is acceptable.
